pairs.evidence: crates/api/src/collective/ingest.rs:116 The plausibility gate runs on each entry before the fold, and the only check after the fold is the min_cases floor. A payload that spreads a claim across many invented task labels (all clamped to `general`) can therefore store one bucket far above MAX_CASES_PER_ENTRY, up to u32 saturation. That admits exactly the over-ceiling count the gate exists to reject.

techniques.evidence: crates/api/src/collective/fold.rs:147 Folded case counts are summed without rechecking the million-case ceiling, so the count ceiling can be bypassed by splitting a claim. Clamp vs reject and malformed vs implausible are otherwise handled correctly (sanitize.rs:56-64). There is also no capture-time floor on generated_at.

crates/api/src/collective/sanitize.rs:101 Cost is re-bucketed at the hub (sanitize.rs:100, fold.rs:172). Latency percentiles are continuous measures, yet they pass through at exact millisecond resolution with no bucketing rule and no stated argument why that precision is safe. The technique's sweep-every-continuous-field rule is not met.

crates/api/src/collective/leaderboard.rs:141 Order is merge, then the source floor, then every user filter, then counts over what survived. held_back is disclosed. The hub re-enforces the case floor at ingest.rs:121, and k comes from hub config, not a request parameter.

crates/api/src/collective/scorecard.rs:45 Classified at the source and clamped at the hub (sanitize.rs:89), with the clamp disclosed in the ack. Gap: the hint argument is always None, so operators have no per-benchmark tag. This is an accuracy gap, not a closure gap.

crates/api/src/collective/scorecard.rs:129 The digest is built from run scorecards and never reads events (digest.rs:95). But the rubric fingerprint hashes a local rubric_id@version, a per-contributor identifier, and ships it. A reader could correlate two digests from one contributor using this field alone.

crates/api/src/collective/digest.rs:95 Runs are always stored locally. Publication is a separate admin operation that reads the store and applies the floor and bucketing on the way out. A preview via GET /digest is possible, and attempts are recorded in a ledger.

crates/api/src/collective/contribute.rs:133 Contributions are POSTed to a hub endpoint that replaces the contributor's set, not proposed as changes to a shared store. The technique's precondition does not hold.

pairs.evidence: crates/core/src/collective/types.rs:77 The wire digest carries a contributor-derived, high-cardinality rubric hash. provenance.rs itself calls this a linkage key too sharp to publish, yet it crosses to the hub and is stored there. The hub therefore holds a per-contributor correlation channel finer than anything it publishes.

techniques.evidence: crates/core/src/collective/types.rs:77 This is an identifying input that ships instead of being consumed locally. By contrast, dataset_version is consumed locally (types.rs:43), a single-run variance is None rather than 0 (merge.rs:337), and the schema is additive with MIN_SCHEMA_VERSION=1.

crates/core/src/collective/merge.rs:333 Cost is bucketed to 2 significant figures before it leaves (privacy.rs:16, merge.rs:332). Latency percentiles go on the wire at exact resolution with no bucketing rule or argument, so the sweep-every-continuous-field rule is unmet.
crates/core/src/collective/merge.rs:323 Sub-floor buckets are dropped, not flagged, and the number withheld is counted. low_confidence is a separate display flag.
crates/core/src/collective/vocab.rs:47 The classifier is total and defaults to general (classify.rs:48). Every wire enum is clamped, and WIRE_CATEGORICALS is checked against the schema by a test.

crates/core/src/collective/merge.rs:364 The top source is winsorized at 0.8, single-source rows are left untouched, and the spread uses the same weights (merge.rs:400). max_source_share and the raw n_cases are both disclosed.
crates/core/src/collective/aliases.rs:83 This context supplies the alias normalization and the vocabulary clamps. The gate itself lives in the API context.
crates/core/src/collective/contribution.rs:123 The hash gates re-POSTs to an endpoint. There is no proposed-change transport.

pairs.evidence: crates/store-firestore/src/collective.rs:97 At consumption, the Firestore decoder repairs a missing or mistyped quality, pass_rate, cost or count into 0 instead of skipping and warning. The resulting zero-case phantom still counts toward n_contributors. Meanwhile a missing string or timestamp aborts the whole collect, so one bad document fails the leaderboard read for every reader.

techniques.evidence: crates/store-firestore/src/collective.rs:122 Both consumption failure modes the technique names are present: zeros substituted into numeric fields (line 97), and a hard failure through collect::<Result> (lines 121-123). Neither skips with a warning.
